text:
The silence of the lighthouse is not an absence of sound, but a presence of memory. As the tide rolls in and out, it seems to carry the weight of the past with it. The iron gallery, once a structure of strength, now feels like a skeleton holding its breath. To stand before it is to feel the passage of time, a slow, heavy current that has no destination but the sea.

The keeper's cottage, though cold, holds a warmth that is the warmth of neglect. The slate roof, once a shield against the elements, now sits like a forgotten roof over a sleeping town. The tin of tea on the shelf is a small relic, a reminder of a life that once lived there. It is a symbol of the routine that has been abandoned, a ritual that no longer needs to be performed.

The maps of the coast, drawn by hand, are a testament to the importance of attention. In an age of digital maps, these old maps remind us of the value of physical presence. Every inlet had a name, and every name had a story. To lose those stories is to lose a piece of our own identity.
